ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Elisabeth of Austria Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for weight loss, fatigue, ankle swelling and dizziness: history, examination with orthostatic vital signs, ECG, blood tests, depression and safety screening, a start to nutrition with thiamine, and an eating disorders psychiatry referral. Concerns: She is frightened of gaining weight and of losing control of her body, but is exhausted and dizzy and knows she cannot go on like this; She does not want anyone, including clinic staff, to discuss her weight or her visits, and fears her illness becoming public; She cannot stay in one place for long and will be travelling for weeks at a time. [S]

tr.td: Thiamine 100 mg tablet, one by mouth daily for 14 days, starting before the meal plan
Cholecalciferol 50 microgram (2,000 IU) capsule, one by mouth daily

Phosphorus 250 mg tablet (potassium and sodium phosphates), one by mouth twice daily with meals for three weeks
Calcium carbonate 1,250 mg (500 mg elemental calcium) tablet, one by mouth daily with a meal
Sertraline 25 mg tablet, one by mouth each morning for two weeks
Sertraline 50 mg tablet, one by mouth each morning

text.paragraph: Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.

tr.td: A prolonged illness in early adulthood with cough, poor nutrition, anemia and exhaustion, which improved with time away by the sea
Restrictive dieting since early adulthood, with single-food meals, a fixed upper weight of 50 kg, tight lacing to a waist of about 50 cm, and hours of walking and gymnastics every day
Gave up horse riding in her forties because of health problems not specified in the cited source
Swelling, bodily pains and sciatica in recent years, called hunger edema in letters from a spa
Mourning and deepening depression since the death of her son five years ago

list.item: Weight loss to a body mass index of 16.0 (47.4 kg at 172 cm), about 6 kg over six months, with fatigue, swelling of both ankles, dizziness on standing, slow pulse and cold intolerance; cause not established at intake; a restrictive eating disorder suspected, with thyroid disease, celiac disease, diabetes, malignancy and adrenal insufficiency to be excluded; eating disorders psychiatry consultation requested: resolved, confirmed [S]

Anorexia nervosa, restricting type, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with compulsive exercise and frequent self-weighing, beginning in early adulthood; complicated at diagnosis by sinus bradycardia, orthostatic dizziness, ankle edema, mild anemia and leukopenia, low glucose, raised ALT and low phosphate after refeeding began: active, confirmed [S]
Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate, with persistent grief for her son, who died five years ago; passive thoughts of death without intent or plan at intake: active, confirmed [S]

Acute viral gastroenteritis, caught from a member of her travelling party, with mild dehydration, orthostatic hypotension and mild hypokalemia; no purging behavior; managed with oral rehydration and potassium; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

Low bone mass (osteopenia) of the lumbar spine and hip after decades of low weight: lumbar spine T-score -2.1, femoral neck T-score -1.8; FRAX 10-year probabilities 6.8% for a major osteoporotic fracture and 1.2% for hip fracture; no fractures: active, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for weight loss, fatigue, ankle swelling and dizziness: history, examination with orthostatic vital signs, ECG, blood tests, depression and safety screening, a start to nutrition with thiamine, and an eating disorders psychiatry referral
One-week medical stabilization check and eating disorders psychiatry consultation
Four-week review: weight, vital signs, electrolytes, bone density, and depression
Twelve-week review: weight restoration, exercise, mood and sertraline
Twenty-one-week review: weight, mood, the gastroenteritis, and care while travelling
Same-day sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Eating disorders psychiatry consultation in one week to confirm the diagnosis, decide the level of care, and lead a multidisciplinary plan

Medical assessment and stabilization: orthostatic vital signs and temperature, ECG, blood count, electrolytes with phosphate and magnesium, glucose, kidney and liver tests, albumin, TSH, CRP, ferritin and vitamin D; admission criteria explained; electrolytes, phosphate and magnesium to be rechecked three to four days after the meal plan starts, then weekly for the first weeks

Refeeding risk: thiamine 100 mg daily before and during the first two weeks, and a starting meal plan of about 1,600 kcal a day in three meals and two snacks, increased by about 200 to 300 kcal every few days

Collaborative safety plan with warning signs, coping steps, people to contact including her travelling companion, the clinic number, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and local emergency numbers abroad; medicines dispensed in small supplies and kept by her companion

Privacy: the chart is flagged as restricted, access is audited, she is booked under a scheduling alias at the first or last appointment of the day, and weights are discussed only in the consulting room

Multidisciplinary outpatient treatment: weekly CBT-E with an eating disorders therapist, a dietitian twice a month, medical review by the primary clinician, and psychiatry review; open weighing at sessions instead of weighing at home; by video when she travels
Compulsive exercise: no gymnastics and walks of no more than an hour a day while weight is restored and the pulse and orthostatic changes are abnormal, with a graded return agreed by the team
Bone health: DXA of the spine and hip, calcium 1,200 mg a day from food and supplement, vitamin D, weight restoration as the main treatment, and repeat DXA in two years

Depression with persistent grief: grief-focused work within therapy; sertraline 25 mg daily, increased to 50 mg after two weeks, once nutrition was under way and the QTc was normal; PHQ-9 at every visit and suicide-risk review at every visit
Medically stable for outpatient care: resting pulse 50 or more, no orthostatic dizziness, and normal potassium, phosphate, magnesium and glucose
Pulse 56, orthostatic changes resolved, electrolytes and glucose normal at four weeks
Weight gain of about 0.5 to 1 kg a week toward a body mass index of at least 18.5
From 47.4 kg (BMI 16.0) to 54.0 kg (BMI 18.3) at twenty-one weeks; still gaining
Depression response (PHQ-9 down by at least 50 percent) by six months
PHQ-9 7 at twenty-one weeks, down 56 percent from 16
Exercise reduced to walks of an hour or less a day while weight is restored, with no gymnastics until the team agrees
Walks of about an hour a day; gymnastics stopped

list.item: Independent; tires on stairs, feels faint on standing quickly, and has cut back on reading and correspondence because she cannot concentrate [S]

Very thin, tall woman dressed in black; guarded, courteous and articulate; mood low, affect constricted; preoccupied with her weight and shape; passive thoughts of being better off dead, without intent or plan; no psychotic features; insight partial [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-02-03: current ideation present, intent absent, plan absent. Passive thoughts of death without intent, plan or past attempts; outpatient care with a collaborative safety plan that works when she travels, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and local emergency numbers abroad, medicines dispensed in small supplies, and review at one week [S]
